info_titulo: About the archive content and our criteria
info_p1: This platform features an archive specialized in original Visual Kei and J-Rock audiovisual material, covering physical formats such as DVDs, Blu-rays, and VHS (VHS tapes are fully ripped for digitalization). Our main goal is the rigorous preservation of the technical, artistic, and visual quality of each release, ensuring the content reaches fans exactly as originally conceived by the artists and their respective record labels in Japan.
info_p2: Have you noticed that some of your DVDs or materials do not contain a main menu? This is completely normal. Within the Japanese record industry, if a disc or material includes only a specific music video, a behind-the-scenes making-of, or exclusive commentary, it is extremely common for it to lack an interactive menu. These editions are factory-designed for direct, automatic playback (autorun mode), maintaining a minimalist, distraction-free aesthetic typical of the Japanese physical market.
politica_p1: To maintain an extremely high standard of quality and exclusivity in our catalog, not just any edition is archived. Special releases are exclusively incorporated under two very strict premises, and remember that the photo shown in each post represents the exact edition you will download:
politica_item1_titulo: Made-to-order / Request Limited Editions (完全受注生産限定盤)
politica_item1_desc: Exclusive materials manufactured only according to the exact number of pre-orders requested by fans.
politica_item2_desc: Special initial release versions containing collectibles, alternate covers, or bonus discs, essential for collectors.
politica_footer: In this way, we ensure a curated space focused on pieces of true historical and collectible value for this music genre community.
guia_titulo: Playback Guide for Digitized DVDs, Blu-rays, and VHS
guia_sub: Follow these simple steps to enjoy your audiovisual material correctly according to its intended use:
guia_paso1_t: Download your DVD, Blu-ray, or VHS
guia_paso1_d: Make sure you have enough storage space on your device and that you have downloaded the compressed file or folder with the original structure (such as VIDEO_TS folders in DVDs or BDMV in Blu-rays).
guia_paso2_t: Are you going to burn it to a physical disc?
guia_paso2_d: If you plan to transfer it to a blank/clean DVD or Blu-ray to play it on a traditional home player, skip all further steps and use video-structure-compatible burning software (like ImgBurn or Nero) to burn the image directly.
guia_paso3_d: If you are going to keep it stored on your External Hard Drive or directly on your PC for software playback, proceed to the next step.
guia_paso4_d: Once you have the file ready, use a compatible media player (such as VLC Media Player or MPC-HC). Follow these steps depending on the format:
guia_sub_dvd_d: For folder-structured DVDs or individual VHS videos, you can simply drag the folder or file directly into the player (or use the open file/folder option).
guia_sub_bluray_d: Go to the top menu in Media, click Open Disc, select the Blu-ray option, and browse for the container folder in the disc device section. Finally, click Play.
guia_sub_mpchc_d: Go to File > Quick Open File... or Open Directory... and select the root folder of the format to automatically read the original contents or menus.

compromiso_p1: At J-Music, we don't just collect; we are dedicated to active preservation. We understand that every era of Visual Kei —from the raw, experimental origins of the 80s to today's visual superproductions— constitutes an invaluable historical treasure that deserves to be safeguarded. Our working philosophy is rigorous and based on absolute respect for the original work.
compromiso_rescate_d: Our workflow is a constant cycle of search and restoration. We do not rely on dubious external sources; we meticulously track the global market ourselves to locate physical copies. When material is scarce or non-existent in digital format, we invest in the direct purchase of DVDs, Blu-rays, and fundamentally, original VHS tapes. We are aware that VHS requires special care: it is impossible to put the original physical format into the hands of every fan, so we assume the technical responsibility of performing a high-fidelity ripping process, ensuring the essence of the recording is not degraded.
compromiso_distribucion_d: Once the material has been digitized, we do not let it get lost on a personal hard drive. Our mission is open dissemination. Therefore, we upload each piece to robust and accessible storage platforms, such as TeraBox. We know stability is key, so every concert, documentary, or music video is meticulously organized, categorized, and when dealing with heavy files, divided into multiple parts. This structure ensures that any community member can perform a stable and successful download.
compromiso_esfuerzo_t: Why this effort in the year 2026?
compromiso_esfuerzo_d: We live in a transitional era where physical media is rapidly disappearing. DVD and tape players are becoming antiques, and the entertainment industry has prioritized the ephemeral. By carrying out this preservation work, we prevent our musical culture from falling into a digital 'black hole'. We are building a living archive, a high-quality public library ensuring that the work of Japanese artists does not vanish alongside its original media.
nosotros_como_funciona_p1: It is essential to clarify our methodology so you understand the value of what is shared here: We are not a store, we do not make sales, nor do we accept custom orders. We are, above all, a self-managed digital preservation log.
nosotros_proceso_intro: Our acquisition process is a detective-like work that occurs in several strict phases:
nosotros_fase1_d: Everything starts on the internet. We spend hours scouring forums, specialized digital markets, and Japanese auction platforms looking for clues about the material we want to preserve.
nosotros_fase2_d: If the material is not available online or existing quality is insufficient, we proceed to purchase the physical copy (VHS, DVD, Blu-ray) directly in Japan. We invest our own resources to import these pieces.
nosotros_fase3_d: We understand that the original format, especially VHS, is delicate. We perform a high-fidelity ripping process, converting the material to modern digital formats.
nosotros_fase4_d: Once processed, we upload each piece to massive storage platforms like TeraBox. We structure downloads into small, stable parts to ensure smooth access.
nosotros_urgencia_t: Why do we do it? The urgency in 2026
nosotros_urgencia_p1: We are facing an inescapable reality: physical media is rapidly disappearing. DVD and VHS players are increasingly scarce, and the entertainment industry has shifted exclusively to the cloud.
nosotros_mision_intro: Our mission makes sense in this context of "analog blackout":
nosotros_mision1_d: Many of the concerts and documentaries we treasure do not exist on any official digital platform. We intervene before information is lost forever.
nosotros_mision2_d: We believe the history of Visual Kei should not belong only to those with capital to buy rare items. Digitizing is our way of democratizing culture.
nosotros_mision3_d: We dedicate time to verify image and sound quality, always seeking the perfect balance between file size and technical fidelity.
nosotros_mision4_d: Every VHS we rescue is a witness to a golden era, serving as a reference for future generations.
nosotros_final_p1: Thank you for visiting our personal log. This effort is constant: every month we continue investing in new copies, ripping processes, and hosting spaces.
nosotros_final_p2: We hope you enjoy this legacy as much as we enjoy sharing these unique pieces with you. The community drives us to keep music and imagery alive.
